subject: orb weaver spider
title: A Wasp Larva Makes a Spider Build a Web for Its Cocoon, Then Eats It

scenes.text: This spider's last web isn't for catching anything.
A wasp left an egg on its abdomen. The larva hatched and fed on the living spider.
For up to two weeks, the spider kept spinning normal webs.
Then, on its final night, it built something else: just a handful of bare lines. No spiral. No glue.
The trigger is chemical. Remove the larva, and the spider still builds that web the next night.
Web finished, the larva kills the spider and hangs its cocoon from the lines its victim built.

description:
A Costa Rican wasp lays its egg on an orb-weaving spider, and the larva feeds on the living spider for one to two weeks while it goes on spinning normal webs.
On its last night the spider builds a completely different web: a few plain lines with no sticky spiral. The larva then kills it and hangs its cocoon from that web. William Eberhard reported it in Nature in 2000; when he removed the larva, spiders still built the cocoon web the following night, so the larva controls the behaviour chemically.
Is this the creepiest parasite yet? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: ITS LAST WEB ISN'T ITS OWN
first_comment: The cocoon web has as few as two lines, against dozens in a normal orb. Which mind-control parasite should we do next?
